title: Midterms: Democrats take Congress, and markets split the difference
dek: Voters handed Democrats the House, the Senate and most governorships; oil slumped, the dollar slipped, and a separate AI-driven equity rout swamped the relief rally.

mood.label: Nervous
mood.explanation: The VIX — the options market's gauge of expected swings in the S&P 500 — closed at 28.18 on 5 November, up about 64% in a week, and CNN's Fear & Greed index sits at 20, "extreme fear", down from 43 a month ago. Credit markets are calmer (high-yield spreads at 3.32 percentage points on 4 November, tighter than the day before) and Reddit chatter is all chips and AI names rather than politics, which says the anxiety is about the tech trade more than the election.

regions.headline: Relief rally on Wednesday, AI rout on Thursday
regions.summary: Stocks rose and the dollar slipped as results came in, but the week ended with the Nasdaq down about 7% as chip and data-centre shares sold off. Treasury yields drifted lower, with the 10-year at 4.90% on 4 November. Oil fell hard on bets that the Iran war could end, which matters more for household budgets than anything Congress will do before January.

regions.headline: European indices firm; politicians welcome, officials wary
regions.summary: Euro-area markets took the result calmly: the CAC 40 rose 2.95% and the IBEX 3.33% over the week, with the euro up 0.59% at $1.12. European politicians publicly welcomed the outcome, but policy analysts warned that tariff powers stay with the White House, so trade relief is not automatic.

regions.headline: Whiplash session, then China outperforms
regions.summary: Asian markets swung from selloff to relief rally on results day. Hong Kong gained 3.57% on the week while Tokyo fell 1.71% and Seoul dropped 5.47% amid the global chip rout. Japanese trading-house chiefs said the vote does not remove uncertainty over US trade policy.

body:
American voters went to the polls on 3 November and handed Democrats control of both chambers of Congress plus a majority of state governorships, in what wire services described as a sharp rebuke to President Trump. Yet the week's biggest market move had little to do with ballots: a global selloff in chip and data-centre shares. Two days on, the honest summary is that the election repriced oil and politics, while an AI reckoning repriced equities.

## What happened

Democrats won both the House and the Senate, [ushering in divided government](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNZVhrSEZna25zZzkxdEROS2w2MGkwWmdJTlY2Y3Z3ZWxnQ1MwVzV1YXlDVkdOZ3NOVE5KOXZaVnhBTlBaTlNVSVd4NjdIbklVVGRNYlhIN2NzN0pPNk52aVJpQ1NERFJwZnJLWlZ3MzdqN0VPbWZvcS1qQjNaQXUtUzJKUkc5bTJ4UWc?oc=5) after voters [delivered a strong rebuke to Trump and Republicans](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxPRFA3Qk9sWVFFclA5aUMzTVlKenJNX25YTU5oenBmQXVqWjlneGxXUWRyZ3FSNE43TmRRcjJnbVEzLXJFazZJTVVMeDVUSE9FRktPQXh6b1FpeWtrbzYyMmFtYThKN3Y2NE9nTUV4a2RQaXpGblMxM2JycTVkTFQ5cG9hV3NObHpnMnFUQ0lxNlVuaHpOR1lUWkxPZ2NZcUctRnNnNjE1NjZEeUZBTWZaYVg4V2lBaDM0?oc=5). Reporting noted Democrats [flipped dozens of Republican seats while Republicans flipped none](https://news.google.?oc=5). In the states, Democrats [won a majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOc2RZSGVFZkpycm1mQ1I2cUJTWDdOTHM2MU95ZUZWUjNzVjllSWVVTDdYZC12RlMwS1FrWF8xOEFsYzNpREdQbEdUN3QxWXhBVnc1YUJDRGNaalhCTS1jRmg4MDJIZGlQMTZSck44VnBkdk50TFNkQUhIaUQzRi1wbkNhOXlyQjBINHYzQUVfRHVzSTMxT0xhUTJJTHA1R3lUbVF6SFd6Mm9ucjVDMjI3bw?oc=5), [after wins in key states](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxNS29BU05tMm5La1pmT0JTSGdpbzk2MFN1VDJjR1ZiYUllemtabkxnQVFBUU41aW0wSC1FLVE5a1ExRUhJRS1zRHVNUWhmS252ZTM0dnE5cXpQZTMxcnlrV3RKUDNNZUIzcjhDOHZZMTV5X2VlLW5LN2V4RVVjWk1nRkFJSQ?oc=5).

Not everything is settled. The Senate races in [Mississippi and Alaska remain too close to call](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxOZFE2MnhLMmZSZVptb3p4TlhDQzBUMEpZWERVaHN2dG1YbTJZWGRKZWZvM1laTzRubG5WLXdkMW93bW80VEhOcjhFRm92TTdJNlQtSGF5bWFkZWZDak54ZVdCYmdrS3dEQ2hvT0dpaGtJQ0tVbnNENFNtRHpDQWhfN3dFZlpaY2NucHBaSFN1NU4xWGpLdXBhMkxBU0tMSDluQ3NET0FQcDdabExT?oc=5), with [vote counting and ranked-choice tabulation still under way](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxPWVZIY1ZfRUpxWHRpZXljbUR2S3NEYXJwcExqR0Y2ZlVLZDNLN2dTekd2SjU5NzJ1cXZ2cEhrRkR1T25YME9SWmRJZnpZLUdyMnRtcFJsYk81QTV3dG1ZOFo5dDJYcC1neVFOSHZEbGIzYk90VXNtdjQwT2J0QUF2SmN0aHVLdWtJY3p4cmtpczR1T0dBaWZjMXZvM3Q?oc=5), and a number of House contests are [still undecided](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxQS1RONkJ6dHJidUNYUGVHaElmbzRGRjBJWTI0VTd5VTJubHY2Q2FRT3JiVFJwbG1FZ0xHV3M3NmpuR3ZUbjZ1RHExdnVqLTZZTWtIRW5ILXZFR2c2clBzZWFIZ2dPUVlfbGQ2MXlreXNuYWlPZllhbDVKakdiQlFMN2hvUUJSaXBXNnlaUWN0RWlHOFQ1dF9CbXduSWhXV18tcGRaOElONG1xNHRka0dka2xPVk9pdHM?oc=5). The new majorities do not take office immediately: Democrats [do not take over Congress until January](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixwFBVV95cUxPSXVNNVhRcEt0ZWhpaW52ZW95U3d6Sk80eXhzc2hsZVFvTmhPNm0zTUhmVjBtRWVOQ19GbDI5bVE0ZnZIME1GQ3daZzdWYnF3LVJGeUtnZkp1cnhaZ001Tlk3WkI5YTJwSlBoNmZrMkhRVGJXb3NIVzJGei1XMEVqc1E0cVpnUjNzUGwtc0pDXy1jQ0VoX1p0cGpEd2dBWTNlZ3ZMNUZ0S0h6WUdHc0h0d2dRVVNqUjhSb3VXMWdmNUUzY3BJdXdJ?oc=5), and one report notes the president [keeps Iran war authority until 3 January](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiZ0FVX3lxTE5hbnFyenQzcmJjb0Z5Mkl1X0Q3dG9fUGp3V3pJSGg0aExvYldaUkJaQ3J6VzRwX2RVV0RzS2xSR29fZ3lGbDF5Zk9uZnBTZ0I0UUJYQ1ZIRFB6Z3licVVxTEdPdUVrQ0k?oc=5).

President Trump said in an interview that he [will accept the election results](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxQZnh6NEFhTFFSOFpKQ2ZaTkVfYk8wblJidGZJSGs5R0kzYmo4UlBQYXJVRDhhRFVrc09zUUMyQXBHWkJ2RGJ4UnI3WXpsTkU3VnZNeGRtd0tRckljMms0THYxZHdLbklueS1vRFZhNERXTnpZaW10dTZuUGJiZzQ1SDBadFdJN2M2cVE?oc=5), and in his first post-election appearance [blamed the losses on Republican candidates, oil prices and his absence from the ballot](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxOcm8yRDN0ODJJUUd4WVlJTjk0Y0Z3ZWM2SFNOZ0pfUTJaUjd1QThhTDRveDdxV0hoZW12WUZKeFp0aUVZQnpucVRHZjZzcHZRVk1NRmRibXdjdW1WSk5VTmc1dGRVOW1CeDNLMzFmVFlUcklENUhGMC00OHdEUHlhZ1dpOWs0SFQzWEx2ZmpwMlJiTGxxVWozaVJWcHBleWU5S0pyU012VzRUcnNLcWFNV19rbzdLbDBpbkdzRUNTU3JZZw?oc=5); the White House also [pointed to weak candidates](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## How markets reacted

The first reaction was relief. World shares [advanced as the result eased political uncertainty](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMie0FVX3lxTFBWZWFDY2tZeDZfbXdVWnE2QWZwVlNpX3NqVm1OdmR0bDBGTlJjU3dJWG5yWEFpSG4tSHVhY2NEeVBsNnllVFQyb0tWRU1naXZQLWN3Tlk4VE1PV3o2cU1tVHFYX1hDT1ZtRkVWUWtYR3JwWFRyTXZIRldDWQ?oc=5), and US stocks rose while [the dollar slid](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxNWHBXeHhrYVhzSEt6VXgyZHNpYm9aSjJqaVpvZy1XX0I0VXJLMjFwUUczWkRNeE5mSktyeURtT2h0YnpndldCZHNHQlIzM01ydExEVnVVVjZkdWRZWTVSOTVUM05QOEh0bEIyS1loeFBpVE5HQXJoanJjTHQ3ODlzdEE2dUdFQ2YxRC12UEU3cjRDZ2xVc09Tb09NOWxPNWtoNllZWlR6ZXBsSDFWaFE?oc=5). Asia had [whiplash, with a selloff giving way to a relief rally](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxNVlRYYzBIU3RjVTEwd1YwX1BWQmpsR1oyeVVLOFFZT1JVNDRJU0JPVFlZb1IyYWZnWGtCZ1Y5ZzNqSkMzbWM0NTYwU0dIbmx4V0xJandodEFGcjB0b3h0c0kwXzczVFE3R3NJdGV5OHlKeUpvTDI0dXhGZW5sTFRPZmw0dG9pRlpvMU8zTXNYTW9fTklJbmUwdXRRbnl5WWI5dTlYaQ?oc=5).

Then the AI trade took over. By Thursday the [Nasdaq sank around 5% as investors ditched chip and data-centre stocks](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihwFBVV95cUxPd0JqeUJIeUF5NWZ0RVUtVDhfSlJCMjc4U1didmsxU2lRZGdJcUZnNk90V0ZkVy1JNVZKRG10WkFySU1lREhqNUs2ZGlWZXhNRXBNMjVKWlJWajg5OWNFdG91V3VRV1B3cEkzSHNOVkFDaXRwbGJKUkRkX2lRdmtqQ0xGSTN5NVU?oc=5), with the index [entering correction territory](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimgFBVV95cUxPM256SDZwbThRbW0xN0pkWGg4eWVoWFlPX2JXRC01UnBNV0EyaGFvdXNRbV8weEc5YmJ6SHVDTHNzQTg2OXFyTFRIcGNEd0ZfbzdNckRKV0FKWV9STFUzZW4wQmhXRFZBTExKN3psSncySmZpMThvX1pQUE1ra0ZCX29KS2doWXRVbmRYdGkzZ0N2Ulhack1BV3FB?oc=5) and the [VIX spiking 39%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiywFBVV95cUxNSExLTTdRNzVJeFp0eTV0ZUlrSy1fbERoSzdkWkN0STBSend4OHhIZ3RpQzUwS0ZZdlVKb0lNYmZyd0FrTUNubXltczB6SXQ0OGVKenFYbHc1NWhlM1RLRHNDVk8tb3ZuNDhSSGZvVktqVWQweWJaYk9yZ04tQ0JObWtJaHdheHJDbnFZS1lpakdaTHZCbFpvVEhWemJoQVVHY3ZFQnZMSUgzN2piM3FHeUIyMXR1c2k5Z3A4VmNKQ2plbjNiNS1jVlQxNA?oc=5). On the week to 5 November the S&P 500 is down 4.75% at 7,353.73 and the Nasdaq Composite down 7.14%. The VIX — a measure of how much movement options traders expect in the S&P 500 — closed at 28.18, up roughly 64% in a week.

Bonds were steady to firmer. The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.90% on 4 November, down from 4.95% the day before; the 2-year was 4.58%. The gap between them, the "yield curve", was 0.32 percentage points — still positive, so longer money costs more than short. The dollar index slipped 0.43% on the week to 101.6, with the euro at $1.12 and the yen at 157.68.

The clearest election-linked move was energy. Crude [slumped as the midterm rebuke raised bets on an exit from the Iran war](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxPQUEyU0pEVG8xTHJtT2xCU0ltcXVTalphM0RNTEZ0UVlCTW5Qbjg4cS1RQnh5QXZnVEZvdnBacmZRM2FhMWJLWXVjU08yNkpvOHZiLTUtSGN0Mk55NGFBNWdxTmR4b3ZBeGNlX3ptUGNaRVFzRzhyNDZodklncGFZaV96cUxHY1Q1ODZWdmpTVWlWRVp4bVdJb0Zrb1pLaXVsUFFySUd4cm40cFphNGZB?oc=5), then [fell below $90 a barrel after Vice-President Vance blamed the defeat on the war](https://news.google.?oc=5); prices [rebounded slightly](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxOTDROS29td1ZxNlFndnlTQnU4LVVwTXg1OW9kemVlQmx4M1pZTFlOd21RNnJhcnBVNENOSEpjT2YyWC1DMVhXcHFpNHBMUlF6Mk9NeVFmV19RVnpZTkl0RVE1YjFYVk5JRFZBVFJQbGtlaVFQS2FCazJKWWNQRUVOaDdNdzBuUU1z?oc=5) later. Brent is down 14.23% on the week at $98.53 and WTI down 11.08% at $90.70.

## What it means for policy

On tariffs, executives told Reuters a Democratic win is [unlikely to ease cost and tariff pressures in the near term](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxNMFREOVI1am9RMmxtb1dOZTc2dFNqaDZLMENlSFQwZEg3SWthaFdPVVV3QXEyMjlKTE5zZHI3Nk1RclhjZWt3SmZuQjNyMVM3c2RLZFo4Z0JEOEZCdXNPZFBPLVpCZnlmUkFBNWE5Zk0zcWFyTTNBZHlMR1FtaFFRVnNXWS04LTlocmtSTEFscG9GTlh6aGd3SC0tVHRmSWtYdnhKWnRqVmNHa0NhaEhkTENiRnJEaWJOREtuOEN1dVRrQQ?oc=5), and a former ambassador argued Congress [could curb the Iran war but not the tariffs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMic0FVX3lxTFBYZXl4MWdyZG1sdUV2VV96cFIycVlnaUxHU1d5dW9rQjlEdnVaWThZb3VGZ3FTOWg1cHBqUzR3VWJNcjRtekV3QnBZOEhVbE1rVlhoX0h3YXBLbmY2ZWl1bnRTa2ZhZ0diaWNQZF9IRmdCV0U?oc=5). Analysts note the [White House still holds significant power on trade](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiywFBVV95cUxQRlNDR3k4bXlCRG0zUmZjRnJHbEItWnVXRFp4c2FoelNKQVlMeXY2dnlmTXcxYXdfR25Da2JzXzV5NW40czRGdzREOUtGMEJONTl4cEtwdkhhM0ZKVlJYVkJZNDFLRWxZNk5OWWkxb013enlleHQybjVPaXo0b2VwQXc2VnU0V2E4N3FvNlFvSWsxcDk1elR2MkNfTGF1TkVVM2FscEdyWXpqX2laT2wwRHd3YUNJRHJkbGRMdkVsVUlYak5KcWlmNE8xSQ?oc=5).

On the Fed, Reuters wrote that the election [stiffens the central bank's guardrails while independence risks remain](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOdkp0QllhLXhJSURNNS1INjdNbjZfRFpWdjFrWHRuc09GeTRFOWlEV0JrQ2tRaExoYTB0R2NFVUtNQVl4bmtuZ0FaUFU5cUtMc2FwWWN1amVNR2xFcjZBTGZwdi0xUGsyRFJOOFhpYUo1OWNrLXJZUkdyeE5QZ3dpcmtpV09faUpwejZHdm9NRGN3dTZxR1NhMkdFdHRtMVZqNUZ5ZTkwRDdiQVlMcGxMUy1B?oc=5), since a Democratic Senate [blocks plans to reshape the Federal Reserve board](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTE9MX0lObGgwbDEwZS1KQURIakRPRGQxZTJ3LVdyUzR5T0E5RlVCZDlsVVI5MlBrS2NtdzBTS2lfeklkVjBCMkNwcVpzOEd2bnZMTHo0TG03RUZnUDRWVGQtVW5WUjQxT3dOdnlfUmxxb1prS3pZQlE?oc=5).

On the public finances, Reuters reports investors are [eyeing the risk of a debt-ceiling standoff](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuwFBVV95cUxNSFJkY2Voejd3d3ZVOXgxOEMtS3U3eXZFUUdDancxUDdiVEEtOW1HMXE2dFhfcTRzR292NTJBNUltNTNhRmVzdTdHLXUtMXoteGdFLTJZNVhlLUs0Zm5CT0lWMVFxM1o0aWxKVUloYnpVNUZZS2VyZmRfZlJRZEs1SWdPUEZ6aGFnbS1XWHRmeXFjS1hMSlFBOTVXWFdFekIwT2tfaU50eTBoVzY0OFk3M3dQQkRrU3B1OHpV?oc=5) — the statutory cap on federal borrowing — with Wall Street [already bracing for a 2027 fight](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxNSWVoa2tsQ0hRd19YTnlyUHNKZTIwZHVqSmFMbkt5WEJXVm1qTnZtR21EVmktUFdXOGx1OHdPNlJxempGZTJwYkVObG5hVVEyRW0tR3R2MHRfLVZPRzEwaXUtNmZMNHpuYUlwSkdCS3JzSFhIQXAtaWxKbFY0M1kwS3FHWUNLLU5mVDRodUN1ME9wdEdwb3Y2OE1IeURBQzhVQnY2X2Z2RQ?oc=5) and commentary warning it is [the one place Democrats can extract concessions, and markets will dislike it](https://news.google.?oc=5).

Democrats themselves have framed the mandate around cost of living, saying the victories [call for a focus on affordability](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxNWGtOZjgxSUQzQ3pnX3dZNFNmOHRndGNWeFlyZTZ5WVVSZktERlprR2k4SHBNUHdSa1M2Q1ZEb2IxQi04dllBSmNLZ041QkdSQjZUcVRQY0RvT2VKZDdLZVdPWFp5SzZfMm9DQnEwQXZGQWNObVJnRC13UGpRcHR1d2tEYVh5cEpT?oc=5), with questions already raised about [how soon they could deliver](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxNOW50ZWlGM09wTDE3X1YtYkQ0WjNBOEFUMDdISnNzME1Gc1B0cTJ4dGdtMjJPd2J6M0VIUTh5YVE4cTJnd3d0dE5wZEgwS3F5MVNpNFEyaEMzM3Q1azVzbm94S01uM3cyREthbW1oamFxLTlkSVU5d1hiYjJSTl9sVHVoSQ?oc=5). Senior Democrats have also called for a [national data-centre moratorium](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## What it means for businesses and households

Three channels matter. Energy: cheaper crude feeds through to fuel and freight, though NPR cautioned against expecting [quick relief at the pump](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxOekxPaHpZcmZobERCQUxZUFQ5Z1kwYzZDRklvZG1SMWtadnNuRXpzbUNZV0ZfNm1xU05Oa1JGblVBZE5aWUtxT3ctaVhJVUVhbEkzdU1sTGJyUGlqOUtLWUNWSXVVUFowUE9Qc0tldkNaME85YmpRVXVLaVlyNktmWkxoaGtoUQ?oc=5). Borrowing costs: nothing in the result has shifted policy rates, with the fed funds rate at 3.88% in October and CPI inflation at 4.0% in September. Import costs: tariff powers sit with the executive, so purchasing teams should not assume relief.

For firms planning capital spending, the sharpest change is local. Voters [rejected data centres in almost every ballot measure](https://news.google.?oc=5), a [nationwide backlash](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxNU1dtLXh4bkZMU0R3X1ZqXzVKNXBjRE1JbkNuQUg5R3o2VEE4SUVEM3lqUFZZOHlKTVkyN2tYUEZIdXJTOWZuVWRlQXY1dl9vVkdTVHZFWkpuajdIX2U5UEtjQ2wwQkx4MnM1SnhpeVZCVU96cXc3U1pBekJXWlAya05CN1Q5QTNmQ2Zyc0Y4WDFLWndvQS1tdHM2eHA5R3pUdW9RUU9UcG5mSk13dUhTQ2t2V1JMWmdLU3c?oc=5) with real consequences for construction, grid investment and the jobs that follow.

## Beyond the US

European politicians [hailed the result as a rebuke of Trumpism](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxOWkc4Y2l6M3hyNnZrSE9sLXQ0NUk1amlDRHRkbkdsbmdUYkZmdWxEaXFiRUotTm44RlNOcmRWbWZUSndfNi1FYTRveVk5ZEhkTUx5Wm16UFNwbU95WHQ1R1hld2RPcWoyNFBtWHBkUGZlaVhxTTl4bmhZN00xcWIwTGJOc24?oc=5), though analysts flagged [Europe's own headaches](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxPVERVVjZpZ29IMHByeE9uQ0tpS1QzNG05VFhWSDJrQnI3Uk4xMFBQZGRqcjgzZDkzN2dOcDNDRXNNLU5nRkdUUVZfTjVYeFFVQ2Y2RGdFRFUyQXB1b0M3OEhRaUV2TjhwR01EbC1UcjR0VGpOSUtadnZPcjlEODF4VlMtQVFkRnEwekoydDlJQXVrNDdoLWhfQ3lpV1g?oc=5) and allies were described as [wary of a backlash](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQSEVYQlFiOVBqUlBBX0hfUnUyZlkxd2NfQVhEOTJZQTNkdk44bFk0YWZFbTNRNHhwZmloTGtYWEFlSkwyZUNZQV9mb0pXdTVBNXNZVUpybHJRSmhMX0lKOFEyRHV0ckYtVGNtQUp5QUVNUWNEQklmbzVZcGRGNWprMExhUlFLM0NqRU5iRmpFc0hlamhwUkhRV1R4dmtfWEwzMDgwdnlfdml6VnBvTEYwT2psUXlZZw?oc=5). European indices held up: the DAX rose 1.1% and the CAC 2.95% on the week.

In Asia, Japanese trading-house chiefs [warned of continued uncertainty](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxQMnpCV0QxV2ZEeGNuUWxYWDJQa2ZRay1VLTl1ZVV5SzZfeTZtNWNDZDJRRFc1YjkzQUZ6VWdZRXFBaW03NWdEYjdFaEg1c0lmeFBoQldTU2czd2d3VmRMVFRDc2ZsYW9QTF9OWFdIVWtzZl9VR0JSY0UzY1BsbjN4bVllckYtVGZlZkVjejBTQlBRVU5acDNuSW5kaFVXNjdZOHQ3THZhd19kZTRnX3c?oc=5), while China [outpaced peers as support measures steadied markets](https://news.google.?oc=5) and separately [blocked a $5.4bn SoftBank robotics deal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxNWU1MYTRpWmVYU2dfWXBkTjR3U3ZERnVWUGtMVkttTjFPT3JPUE43NUdIRE1KcHVzcEpRNHpDaHdHOXEzbHQxcEJEVkNYNGRnY2lhV0ctZFRvb19adzJLcENWLXlINk1DRkNSUl9LQWlrVlRDaFVhb3dSVWF6c1l3Y3NGd3dQdFR5Z2ZLQWlvMFNhV1dtQVIyNVF2SFQycm9iS1Y4dQ?oc=5). Hong Kong gained 3.57% on the week; Seoul fell 5.47%.

## Market mood

Fear dominates, but not the political kind. Fear & Greed is at 20 ("extreme fear") against 43 a month ago, the VIX is near 28, yet high-yield credit spreads — the extra yield demanded to lend to riskier companies — narrowed to 3.32 points on 4 November, which is not the signature of a funding scare. Reddit's most-discussed tickers are overwhelmingly semiconductor and AI names and broad index funds; as an unverified mood gauge, that points to a tech-positioning shakeout rather than election panic.

## What to watch next

The remaining Senate and House calls, the lame-duck session before January, the next CPI print and the Fed's December meeting.
